raw:
The second half of orientation consists of examples rather than speeches. Kira distributes a failed border petition and shows where its author assumed authority the office did not possess. Windwhisper reviews the first month’s schedule, including Monday’s written recommendation and a supervised committee simulation later in the week.

Orientation ends shortly after the tenth bell.

The public dueling board stands beside the path to the octagon. Today’s challenges have been written in chalk beneath the permanent rankings:

*Eleventh Bell — First Board*  
*Ashara vel Kothren, Rank One*  
*Merek Solane, Rank Three*  
*Declared weapons: single blade / paired blades*

A smaller note records Solane’s change from spear to paired blades yesterday afternoon. The bout has not begun.

You reach the dueling ground while the spectators are still gathering. Low stone terraces overlook the octagon’s packed earth, and you take an open place with a clear view. Streamers tied to the western posts pull steadily east in the changing wind.

Rashid stands near the front rail, his morning practice clothes replaced by another immaculate coat. Ysolde watches from the upper terrace, still enough that only her white hair moves in the wind. Neither draws you into conversation.

Ashara enters carrying one long wooden practice blade. She has retied her black hair, and the morning’s dust has been washed from her ember-red skin. Across from her, Merek Solane wears the white training coat of the Military track. At the referee’s signal, broad white wings manifest behind him. He draws two short practice blades whose warded edges shine gold.

The referee raises one hand.

“Three scoring contacts or a yield. Restricted force. Begin.”

Solane moves first. His wings drive him across the packed earth in a sudden low rush, one blade pressing Ashara’s guard outward while the other strikes her shoulder. Blue ward-light flashes across her coat.

“First touch, Solane.”

They reset.

Ashara gives ground during the second exchange, keeping her single blade between both of his. Solane attempts the same crossing attack. This time she steps inside it. Her hilt catches one wrist; the length of her blade turns and lands across his ribs.

“Second touch, vel Kothren.”

The third exchange lasts longer. Solane stays on the ground, using his wings to check and alter his momentum without committing to flight. His paired blades keep Ashara’s weapon occupied until a quick reversal reaches her side.

“Third touch, Solane. Two to one.”

The crowd shifts closer to the rail.

Ashara resets without looking toward the terraces. Heat rises visibly from her shoulders, wavering against the pale stone beyond her. When the referee begins the fourth exchange, she stops pursuing Solane’s retreats. She holds the center and makes him circle.

He moves toward the western edge. The east wind catches his open wings, forcing him to shorten one step. Ashara’s tail braces against the turn as she pivots. Her blade strikes the outside of his thigh before his second weapon can close.

“Fourth touch, vel Kothren. Two to two.”

For the final exchange, gold light runs along both of Solane’s blades. Ashara’s answering magic is smaller: a red flare beneath the skin of her sword arm, drawn inward rather than thrown.

Solane attacks from above. The wind pulls at one wing as he descends near the western boundary. Ashara slips under the first blade, takes the second against her guard, and turns the collision into a short strike against the center of his chest.

The ward on his coat flashes brilliant blue.

“Final touch, vel Kothren. Bout.”

Noise rolls across the terraces. Ashara lowers her weapon, breathing hard enough that steam lifts from her collar. Solane’s manifested wings fade. He presses a fist to his chest where the ward caught the blow, then offers her his forearm. She grips it once.

At the ranking board, an Academy clerk records the result without changing the order: Ashara remains first.

Spectators begin filing back toward the quadrangle. Ashara stays beside the octagon long enough to cool down and collect her practice gear, while Rashid waits near the rail.
